PRINCIPLE: Content distribution is the actual leverage, not technical quality. Build shitty software → get a payment link out → spam viral content → fix based on what paying customers complain about.

SOURCE: Roy Lee (Cluely) video 'How to get so Unbelievably Ahead it feels illegal', March 12 2026. $120M company at 21 by cheating on Amazon interview, recording it, going viral.

NED'S REACTION: 'I agree I need this skill exactly' — said immediately after posting Pixel Office on LinkedIn and realizing 'that was easier than I expected, wasn't scary.' The connection clicked: fear of public failure was the only blocker, and the first post proved it was overblown.

KEY INSIGHTS:
- Under-28 + 2h/day scrolling = algorithmic model for virality baked in brain
- Distribution > product quality. '11M views while product didn't even work'
- 'Nobody's building anything. Nobody has any purchase links out.' The bar is actually low.
- Content is the button. Pressing it once is scary. Spamming it becomes mechanical.

APPLICATION FOR NED:
- Marketing background + builds fast = exact profile Roy describes
- Already has 'the button' — demonstrated it with Pixel Office LinkedIn post
- Gap: volume. Roy spammed 100+ videos. Ned has posted once.
- Strategy: face replacement via Kling AI removes identity exposure risk
